reviews.evidence: The page now explicitly uses the real scaled-reflector arithmetic and local target/separate-panel coefficients. The current real supplier Statement gives kappa_m including target zero writes and b_m=(1+u)c_m+3u for separate blocks; the local two-sided lemma Facts F1 and steps 1.1–2.1 compose these with the right update as alpha=a+b+ab. The finite Francis procedure step 4 requires mu<1, successful range operations and an actual certificate, retaining inconclusive otherwise. The page does not import a false 3 gamma bound or assume shift convergence.

Actual page-level transfer has two parts: the complex wrapper invokes the canonical scaled complex Householder procedure/lemma, and pseudospectrum membership Facts A1 invokes the successful SVD backward bound and absolute-error corollary. Current supplier Statements supply eta_H/separate-block coefficients and the final modulus-readout allowance. The consumer explicitly retains deflation, shifted-input formation, arithmetic and readout allowances, and undecided on budget exhaustion or unavailable bounds; no relative accuracy or unconditional convergence transfers.

Definition calls exactly the supplier Householder branch on [x B], preserves the scaled real-component norm, separately scaled phase modulus, sequential dots and target overwrite, and returns its stored vector/coefficient. Its external-polynomial-vector use selects the supplier separate-block application without overwriting an unrelated column. Facts F1 and proof 1.1 use the finite sequence/failure branch; breakdown relabels nonpositive norm, without asserting success there.

Definition and Facts F2 use the supplier exact representative H(v)=I-2vv*/(v*v), target coefficient eta_H and separate-block coefficient. Proof 1.2 only invokes this on success with nonzero stored v; the supplier explicitly gives unitary representative and local bounds on successful no-underflow calls under its active-dimension hypothesis. This confirms the stated proof-backed interface, without treating rounded dense updates as unitary or granting bounds to failed calls.

Consumer initialization step 1 and chase step 4 call the supplier real-only procedure on the specified target column and trailing panel. Supplier Definition fixes sequential scaling/norm, rank-one multiplication order, target overwrite, stored exact reflector and range failure. Consumer Facts F3 and proof 1.1 use this finite procedure only; the right update and two-sided certificate are specified separately and no local similarity theorem is inferred from the procedure itself.

Consumer Definition applies the supplier model to every scalar operation, including six-real-operation complex products and separately rounded real operations. Facts F1/proof 1.2 use its finite-or-first-range-failure convention. Underflow, invalid operations and overflow remain explicit failures; exact product representations and outward certificate allowances remain distinct from rounded dense factors or residual diagnostics.

The source lemma gives the actual real target coefficient kappa_m and separate-block b_m, not a universal two-sided bound. Consumer step 4 uses these through lem-two-sided-scaled-householder-similarity-error, selecting actual target-overwrite versus external-vector separate-panel use, and forms alpha=a+b+ab for each initialization/chase update. It requires mu<1 and range success and withholds a certificate otherwise. This is a transitive coefficient interface, not an extra termination premise.

Consumer Statement requires an already certified |s_hat-sigma_min(zI-A)|<=delta. Facts A1 and proof steps 1.1/2.1 use the supplier successful nearby-factorization/absolute-error interface conditionally, including all local arithmetic and deflation hypotheses. The current corollary adds epsilon_read for rounded complex modulus and excludes budget-exhausted outputs; consumer explicitly includes that readout and any shifted-input formation error in delta. Its inside <=epsilon/outside >epsilon tests preserve the closed-boundary convention, with all other cases undecided.

Supplier Statement provides exact orthogonal H(v), target-overwrite discrepancy kappa_m and separate-block b_m=(1+u)c_m+3u on successful real r=m calls, with mu<1. Consumer Statement/Facts F1 selects a=kappa_m for actual target or a=b_m otherwise. Proof 1.1 embeds left error; 1.2 uses same row-dot/real-coefficient/product majorants on the specified right order, giving b_m(1+a), and 2.1 transports error by the exact reflector. Thus alpha=a+b+ab includes both sides and target writes, with identity E=0.

Supplier Statement provides unitary H(v), target eta_H(m), separate-block b_m=(1+u)c_U+3u and adjoint right bounds for successful canonical complex calls under (m-1)u<1. Consumer imposes stronger mu<1 and uses exactly those coefficients in Statement/Facts F2. Proof 1.2 notes the right kernel reverses scalar operand association while retaining the same norm majorants; alpha=a+b+ab follows. External-polynomial-vector panels avoid target overwrite; failures receive no bound.

Nonlogical curriculum prerequisite only in the present consumer. Read both page summaries and the supplier Milstein Definition: deterministic-grid Taylor correction uses iterated Ito integrals and commutative-noise reduction. Scanned all current batch30 item bodies for every batch9 item ID: none is used. Read adaptive Euler Definition and predictable-grid moment/error Facts/Proof: actual transfer is from Euler–Maruyama and stopping-time Ito suppliers, and endpoint-dependent refinement expressly has no predictable-grid error certificate. No Milstein order-one, area-sampling or weak-order claim is imported by this page edge.

Actual page transfer is the operationwise real arithmetic definition, used by the Arnoldi, CG-gap and GMRES-recomputation Facts/Proof. Supplier specifies nearest-even zero/normal successes, rounded positive square root, per-operation relative error and first range-failure. Consumer statements impose the relevant nu<1, gamma_n<1, 2u<1 and positivity/success conditions; page preserves normalization breakdown/inconclusive branches. No Cholesky, direct-QR or least-squares stability conclusion is transferred.

Actual transfer is confined to the sparse GMRES cost proposition: supplier canonical CSR Definition identifies s=nnz(A), validated exact matvec visits every stored entry, and cost theorem gives O(s) for square nonempty-row records. Consumer Statement explicitly requires canonical n>=1 representation with every row nonempty and exact arithmetic. Facts F1–F3/proof 1.1 use precisely that interface; page excludes runtime/convergence and memory-bandwidth conclusions.

Nonlogical page prerequisite retained for comparison with iterative methods. Read both summaries, the supplier Richardson Definition and A=D-L-U convention. Scanned all current batch34 item bodies against every batch18 item ID: no such logical invocation occurs. The consumer CG, Arnoldi, Lanczos and GMRES claims use their named Krylov/spectral/rounding suppliers, not Richardson/Jacobi/GS/SOR convergence. This disposition confirms context only and asserts no stationary-algorithm transfer or broad supplier-proof review.

Supplier Definition provides successful-operation relative error, positive correctly rounded square root and component divisions. Consumer Statement requires all products/partial sums/square roots/divisions succeed, nu<1, gamma_n<1, 2u<1 and t_j>0. Facts F2 and proof 1.2–1.3 use exactly these to bound update/coefficient errors and beta>=(1-u)sqrt(1-gamma_n)||w||, then the normalization error. Zero normalization is breakdown; a failed hypothesis is inconclusive. Dot-product theorem remains a separate declared supplier.

Consumer Statement specifies successful real row dots and one rounded product plus addition/subtraction per vector update, nu<1 and 2u<1. Supplier Definition supplies those operations and gamma_k, with no gradual underflow guarantee. Facts F1/proof 1.2 derive the gamma_2 update bounds from the two relative errors; proof 1.1 gap identity uses actual stored alpha and does not assume exact CG scalars. No unconditional termination or true-residual monotonicity is imported.

Facts F2 and proof 3.1 use the supplier relative error specifically for the successful subtraction b_i-Ax_hat_i, yielding u|b_i-Ax_hat_i|. Rounded row-dot error is separately supplied by Facts F3. The exact-coordinate residual algebra and norm bound do not require an accurate least-squares solve; computed y remains explicit. Consumer retains the no-range-failure and gamma_n domain convention and makes no claim for failed residual recomputation.

Supplier Definition permits duplicates/stored zeros generally, but its canonical branch uniquely stores nonzeros and yields s=nnz(A). Consumer Statement explicitly selects this branch and square n>=1 with every row nonempty. Facts F1/proof 1.1 use that identification and row partition, avoiding replacement of stored count by nnz for general records.

Supplier Definition validates finite dimensions/indices and on valid exact-field data initializes outputs then performs one multiply/add for each stored entry. Consumer exact-arithmetic canonical square matrix satisfies these validity conditions. Facts F2/proof 1.1 count one such call per Arnoldi column; at earlier breakdown it counts only performed columns. No floating-point or convergence property is inferred from the algorithm.

Supplier Statement bounds validation/control by O(n+s+1), and for square n>=1 with a stored entry in every row obtains s>=n and O(s) work. Consumer explicitly assumes each row nonempty and canonical s=nnz(A); Facts F3/proof 1.1 sum at most m calls to O(ms). Remaining O(m^2 n) orthogonalization/projected work and O(mn) Krylov storage are locally counted, excluding stored input matrix as stated.

Supplier Statement assumes Countable Choice, bounded A between real/complex Hilbert spaces and lambda>0, and gives ||R_lambda g||<=||g||/(2sqrt(lambda)). Consumer explicitly assumes Countable Choice, constructs bounded compact diagonal A on real ell2 in verification 1.1, and selects lambda=N^-2>0. Facts F7/step 3.1 use delta/(2sqrt(lambda))=1/2 N^-2nu; step 2.1 independently computes the exact filtered e_N noise achieving that value. No source-condition or compact-convergence conclusion is supplied by this lemma.
